content.purpose: Use the compact form when typing and the readable form when writing something down.
content.mentalModel: Most GNU commands accept two spellings of the same option: a single dash with one letter, and two dashes with a word. -a and --all mean exactly the same thing. Single-letter options can be grouped behind one dash, so -l -a -h becomes -lah. Long options cannot be grouped, but they are self-documenting, which is why scripts you will read again should use them.

demonstration.explanation: Shows hidden entries as well. The same result as ls --all.
Three options grouped: long format, all entries, human-readable sizes. Order does not matter here.

remember: -a and --all are usually the same option in two spellings
Single-letter options group behind one dash: -lah
Long options do not group, but they explain themselves
